 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajnish Bhatnagar
 Order
This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No.451/2018, under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Tilak Nagar, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Learned APP for the State appears on advance notice and accepts notice.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 23.07.2017 according to Sikh rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
One child was born out of the said wedlock.
After the marriage, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since 22.4.2018.

On 02.11.2021,
the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against 4.
Counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the MOU dated 23.03.2022
Copy of the said settlement is placed on record.

Accordingly, the petition under Section 13-B(2) of the HMA Act was allowed and the marriage of the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was dissolved vide decree dated 29.10.2022 passed by the Judge, Family Court-02, West District, Tis Hazari Courts.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Delhi.
The copy of the decree is already on record.

sentences.text: Petitioners and respondent no.2 are present in Court today and have been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
As per settlement, today, Rs. 3.5 lacs have been handed over to respondent no.2 in cash.
Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
6. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question be quashed.
7. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.451/2018,
under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Tilak Nagar, Delhi, and the proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.

It is directed that parties shall remain bound by the MOU dated 23.03.2022.
8.
The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J FEBRUARY 16, 2023/ib
